points.text: Effect of group-relative term on individual vs collective reward trade-offs not analysed
Related work omits earlier GAIL-based driver behavior modeling papers
No comparison to controllable traffic generation baselines like CTG, LCTGen
Prior group-relative RL fine-tuning for driving (Gen-Drive) not discussed
No dedicated covariate-shift analysis comparing SFT and RIFT under matched conditions
Distance-threshold CBV identification unjustified; no sensitivity or TTC-based comparison
Non-standard metrics; no evaluation on Waymo Sim Agent Challenge or its baselines
AV evaluation in Table 2 confounds sim agents and planners
CBV identification misses intersection vehicles on different routes with high collision risk
Realism evaluated in simple conservative CARLA; should use Waymo Sim Agent ground truth
Realism measured by normality and target-speed distance, not against human logs
WOSAC mis-described as controllability benchmark
Novelty over RS/RTR unclear; components exist; baselines are indirect re-implementations
Dual-stage framework is standard recipe; pre-training is downloaded checkpoint
Controllability not compared against any conditional generator
CAT-K and TrafficRLHF dismissed but not run as baselines
Theory uses binary reward, no KL; dual-clip guarantee not derived; contraction assumed
Inaccurate supporting citations for LLM pre-train/fine-tune and REINFORCE
Missing references on RL traffic simulation and diffusion policy optimization
KL removal and group-relative advantage not isolated by ablation
RIFT vs GRPO-Pluto differences mostly within one standard deviation
Training stability claim lacks learning curves
Seed semantics unstated; no training-seed variance
Evaluation on only ten dev routes; block rates reflect few events
No significance tests or confidence intervals
Baselines supervised by PDM-Lite, which is also the evaluated AV
Baseline tuning budgets not stated
RL baselines are adversarial generators, not realism-oriented comparators
Policy distribution for scoring head, importance ratio, normalization epsilon and N_ref undefined
Training reward overlaps with evaluation metrics
Controllability shown by a single reward-weight change
Dual-clip Eq. 8 as printed zeroes gradients for positive advantages
Table 3 delta missing minus sign
CBV selection rule inconsistent between Sec. 4.1 and App. B.2
'Consistently outperforms all baselines' contradicted by Table 1
PlanT results in Table 2 contradict near-optimal wording
Head-only fine-tuning buried in caption; multimodality preservation trivial by construction
Abstract and results claims stronger than tables, incl. safety-interactivity balance
Variance, seeds and evaluation set size hidden in captions and appendix
Small ML contribution with limited generality for ICLR; no second domain or model
Typos: LR notation, GPRO, iteraction, missing minus sign
2D-TTC/ACT safety metrics inconsistent with interpretation; aggregation undefined
More benign scenarios not shown to give more reliable, discriminative AV evaluation
Near-optimal AV evaluation claim fails for PlanT
Controllability shown with one scalar knob; no response sweep
High uncomfortable-rate for RIFT hidden in appendix undercuts realism
Signed mean jerk is not a comfort measure
Assumes full observability and single CBV; multi-CBV untested
nuPlan-to-CARLA domain shift and sim-to-real gap not quantified
Realism measured by normality and target speed, not human behavior
AV-evaluation reliability inferred from better AV scores; explained by yielding CBVs
Reliability claim fails for PlanT
KL removal and group advantage not ablated
GRPO-Pluto within noise on most metrics
No learning curves supporting stability
Theorem A.4(c) unsupported; theory does not guarantee stable learning
Evaluation on dev10 with 3 seeds; quantized block rates
No significance tests, CIs or training-seed variance
'Consistently outperforms all baselines' false on several metrics
Aggressive reward raises TTC/ACT, contradicting higher-is-safer reading
Table 3 missing minus sign
Signed mean jerk not a comfort statistic
